Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-1519", "title": "Premature Babies", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Almost 1 of every 10 infants born in the United States are premature, or preemies."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "A premature birth is when a baby is born before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Important growth and development happen throughout pregnancy - especially in the final months and weeks."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Because they are born too early, preemies weigh much less than full-term babies."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "They may have health problems because their organs did not have enough time to develop."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Problems that a baby born too early may have include: Breathing problems Feeding difficulties Cerebral palsy Developmental delay Vision problems Hearing problems Preemies need special medical care in a neonatal intensive care unit, or NICU."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They stay there until their organ systems can work on their own."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5632", "title": "Histoplasmosis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Histoplasmosis is an infection caused by a fungus called Histoplasma ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This fungus is common in the central and eastern United States, especially around the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can also be found in parts of Central and South America, Africa, Asia, and Australia."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It lives in the environment, especially in soil that contains large amounts of bat or bird droppings (poop)."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "You get histoplasmosis by breathing in Histoplasma fungal spores from the air."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It usually happens after you have been doing an activity that disturbs the soil, such as farming, construction, and landscaping."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This means that you cannot get the infection from another person or an animal."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "What are the symptoms of histoplasmosis?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Most people who breathe in the spores never have any symptoms."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "If you do get symptoms, they usually start between 3 and 17 days after you breathe in the spores."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The symptoms may include: Fever Cough Fatigue Chills Headache Chest pain Body aches For most people, the symptoms of histoplasmosis will go away within a few weeks to a month."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "However, some people can have symptoms that last longer, especially if their infection becomes severe."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Certain people are more likely to get a severe infection: People who have weakened immune systems , for example from: Having HIV Having had an organ transplant Taking medicines which weaken your immune system, such as chemotherapy and steroids Infants Adults age 55 and over Severe histoplasmosis can develop into a long-term lung infection."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It can also spread from the lungs to other parts of the body, such as the central nervous system (the brain and spinal cord)."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This is known as disseminated histoplasmosis."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "To find out if you have histoplasmosis, your health care provider: Will ask about your symptoms and your medical and travel history Will do a physical exam Will likely order a blood, urine, or tissue test to look for signs of the fungus May order a chest x-ray or CT scan of the lungs What are the treatments for histoplasmosis?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "For some people, the symptoms of histoplasmosis will go away without treatment."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "But you will need treatment if you have severe histoplasmosis in the lungs, chronic histoplasmosis, or an infection that has spread to other parts of the body."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "That treatment would be with prescription antifungal medicines."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "In some cases, you may need to take the medicines for 3 months to 1 year."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1499", "title": "Hormones", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Hormones are your body's chemical messengers."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They travel in your bloodstream to tissues or organs."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They work slowly, over time, and affect many different processes, including: Growth and development Metabolism - how your body gets energy from the foods you eat Sexual function Reproduction Mood Endocrine glands, which are special groups of cells, make hormones."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The major endocrine glands are the pituitary, pineal, thymus, thyroid, adrenal glands, and pancreas."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "In addition, men produce hormones in their testes and women produce them in their ovaries."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It takes only a tiny amount to cause big changes in cells or even your whole body."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "That is why too much or too little of a certain hormone can be serious."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Laboratory tests can measure the hormone levels in your blood, urine, or saliva."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Your health care provider may perform these tests if you have symptoms of a hormone disorder ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Home pregnancy tests are similar - they test for pregnancy hormones in your urine."}]}, {"id": "MLP-7807", "title": "Post-COVID Conditions (Long COVID)", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What are post-COVID conditions (long COVID)?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) is an illness caused by a virus."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Many people get better within a few days or weeks after being infected with the virus."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They may: Have symptoms that linger for weeks, months, or even years Seem to recover from COVID-19 but then see their symptoms return Develop new symptoms or new health conditions within a few months of having COVID-19 There are several other names for post-COVID conditions."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But it can also be called long-haul COVID, long-term effects of COVID, chronic COVID, post-acute COVID-19, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC)."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Who is more likely to develop post-COVID conditions (long COVID)?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Anyone who had COVID-19, whether it was severe or mild, can have long-lasting symptoms."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "But you are at higher risk of post-COVID conditions if you: Had severe COVID-19 illness, especially if you were hospitalized or needed intensive care."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Had underlying health conditions before you got COVID-19."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Had multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS) during or after COVID-19."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "MIS is a rare but serious condition in which different body parts become inflamed."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "What are the symptoms of post-COVID conditions (long COVID)?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Post-COVID conditions do not affect everyone the same way."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "They can cause various types and combinations of symptoms in different people."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The symptoms may affect different parts of the body, for example: General symptoms, such as fatigue and fever Respiratory symptoms, such as trouble breathing and cough Heart symptoms, such as chest pain and palpitations Neurologic symptoms such as trouble thinking and concentrating (\"brain fog\"), headaches , and sleep problems Digestive symptoms such as diarrhea and stomach pain Some people may have a wide variety of symptoms that are similar to those of other conditions, such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Most people's symptoms slowly improve over time."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "But for some people, the symptoms can last weeks, months, or longer."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Sometimes the symptoms are severe enough to result in disability ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "How are post-COVID conditions (long COVID) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "There is no specific test for post-COVID conditions."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "To find out if you have a post-COVID condition, your provider: Will ask about your medical history."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "This includes asking if you have had a diagnosis of COVID-19, either based on a positive test, symptoms, or exposure."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Some of the symptoms of post-COVID conditions may be hard to explain."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "The results of blood and imaging tests may be normal."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "And people who have unexplained symptoms may sometimes be misunderstood by their providers."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "So it can take some time to get a diagnosis."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "What are the treatments for post-COVID conditions (long COVID)?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "There is no specific treatment for post-COVID conditions yet."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "You and your provider can work together to create a personal care plan to manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Can post-COVID conditions (long COVID) be prevented?"}, {"id": "S030", "text": "The best way to prevent post-COVID conditions is to avoid getting COVID-19."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Staying up to date with vaccines (including boosters) against COVID-19 can help prevent COVID-19 infection and protect against severe illness."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1454", "title": "Genes and Gene Therapy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Genes are sections of DNA in your cells that are passed down (inherited) from your parents."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You inherit two copies of each gene, one from each parent."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Genes carry information that controls what you look like and how your body works."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are about 20,000 genes that provide instructions for making proteins, which your body needs to work correctly."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some genes don't make proteins themselves but instead help control how other genes work."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "They act like switches, turning other genes on or off."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This means they help decide when, where, and how much of a protein is made in your body."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Changes in your genes are also called gene variants or mutations."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "These changes can be inherited, occur as you age, or result from environmental factors such as chemicals or radiation."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Often, these changes have no effect, but sometimes, even a small change in the DNA can alter the instructions for making proteins."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "If genes don't make the right proteins, or don't make them correctly, this can cause a genetic disorder ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Gene therapy uses genes to treat or prevent disease by correcting genetic problems."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It works by changing your genetic material, rather than relying on traditional treatments like medicine or surgery."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "New genetic material can be delivered into cells in two main ways: ex-vivo treatment ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Cells are removed from your body, modified by adding genetic material, and then placed back into your body."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Genetic material is delivered directly into your body, often through an injection."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "A common form of gene therapy involves inserting a normal gene to replace an abnormal gene."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Other approaches include: Repairing an abnormal gene Altering the degree to which a gene is turned on or off Newer techniques offer different ways to correct genetic problems: Genome editing (also called gene editing)."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Instead of adding new genetic material into cells, this approach changes the DNA that's already in your cells."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "This promising technique is still being studied and may soon be used to treat genetic disorders."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Cell-based gene therapy combines gene therapy and cell therapy."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "An example of this would be CAR T cell therapy."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Cells, which are often immune system cells, are genetically altered to help treat a disease and then introduced into the body."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Gene therapies are currently only approved to treat a small number of diseases, such as: Leber congenital amaurosis , an inherited eye disorder."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Spinal muscular atrophy , a genetic muscle disorder."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "What are the risks and challenges of gene therapy?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "While gene therapy holds great promise, it comes with risks and challenges."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Studies are still ongoing to ensure these treatments are safe and effective."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Some challenges include: Immune system reactions."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Your body may see the new material as a threat and react to it."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Changes to DNA could affect other genes in harmful ways."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Gene therapies are often expensive and are not widely accessible."}]}]
